how.title: How to use Image to Prompt
how.subtitleP1: AI Image Describer is a Chrome extension that turns any picture into a clean text description and a ready-to-use prompt for creative work in seconds. It is a fast image describer that lives right in your browser, so you can describe an image right inside your normal browser workflow without opening another tab, signing up, or pasting links into ten different tools.
how.step1: Pin AI Image Describer to your Chrome toolbar.
how.step2: Click the icon and upload or paste a picture to describe this photo.
how.step3: Or right-click any photo on any website and run the analysis directly from the context menu.
how.promptSnippet: If you have ever stared at an image and could not find the words, ai image describer does the work for you. Drop in a picture, and the tool returns a sharp prompt for this scene that pastes straight into Nano Banana, Midjourney, DALL·E, Stable Diffusion, or any picture generation model.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: AI Image Describer in the browser—plain answers about image-to-prompt and the Chrome extension.
faq.q1: What does AI Image Describer actually do when you ask it to describe this image?
faq.a1: It reads visual content and returns a clean description-to-prompt you can copy and reuse.
faq.q2: What should I do if my request is exactly "make a description about this picture for an AI-generated part"?
faq.a2: Paste or upload your image. The service reads the picture and returns a concise, objective visual description you can drop straight into an image-model prompt—subjects, layout, lighting, and style cues.
faq.q3: Can I use it as picture-to-prompt writing for Midjourney or DALL·E?
faq.a3: Yes. It works as an AI photo describer for popular models, and the describe-this-image flow handles pictures-to-prompt one at a time.
faq.q4: Does it save my prompts somewhere?
faq.a4: Yes. The extension keeps a local history of your describe results so you can revisit a prompt anytime. The history stays in your browser—not on someone else’s cloud.
faq.q5: Does it work on any picture?
faq.a5: It supports common formats like PNG, JPG, and WebP.
faq.q6: Can I use it for references?
faq.a6: Yes. Many people use AI Image Describer with saved references, inspiration boards, layouts, visual research, and creative material from around the web.
faq.a7: No account needed. Install the extension, click the icon, and start right away—no email, no card, no waiting before you get results.

BlogAiPromptExamples.h1: AI image prompt examples that actually work
BlogAiPromptExamples.intro: Strong AI image prompts read like a tiny creative brief: subject, environment, light, color, lens or format, and style. Weak prompts stop at “cinematic, 8k, detailed”—they give the model too many equally likely directions.
BlogAiPromptExamples.structureP: Start with who or what owns the frame, then place them in a setting. Add one or two lighting sentences (direction, softness, color temperature). Name materials and textures when they matter. Close with stylistic guardrails—film stock, painterly vs photographic, era—so the model does not drift.
BlogAiPromptExamples.beforeAfterP: Before: a bag of adjectives. After: a short stack of concrete cues tied to composition and mood. You can still iterate; you are just iterating from a prompt that already encodes the scene you liked.
BlogAiPromptExamples.h2_tool: Image → prompt as a starting point
BlogAiPromptExamples.toolP: When you have a reference but not the words, image-to-prompt turns pixels into language you can edit. Paste the draft into Midjourney, SDXL, or any tool you use—then adapt tokens to what that engine respects.
